key_insight: Retinal OCT models can identify biomarker presence yet struggle to localize findings; OCT-specific fine-tuning raised grounding F1 from 23.7% to 33.9%.
clinical_relevance: Reliable localization could make AI-reported retinal findings more verifiable, but these results do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Introduced RetinaGroundBench: 815 OCT B-scans with 4,537 ophthalmologist-annotated boxes spanning 13 biomarkers and 8 diseases.
Proposed AggIoU to evaluate lesion coverage by the union of overlapping predicted boxes.
Evaluated 27 open-source MLLMs and developed RetGrounder, an 8B model fine-tuned with OCT grounding and textual information.
evidence_signal: The best general-purpose model achieved 23.7% macro grounding F1 despite biomarker-presence balanced accuracy reaching 73%; RetGrounder achieved 33.9% F1, a reported 43% relative improvement.
watch_item: Grounding performance remains limited, and the abstract does not establish external clinical validation or patient-outcome benefits.
paper_title: A Visual Grounding Benchmark for Retinal OCT with Multimodal Large Language Models
